description: Easily generate and modify .docx files with JS/TS with a nice declarative API. Works for Node and on the Browser.

latest_release.body:
9.15.3 makes `patchDocument` faster on large documents. It searched the document for each placeholder in a way that slowed down quadratically as the document grew, so patching documents with many paragraphs and placeholders took much longer than it should. The search now runs in linear time and finds the same paragraphs in the same order (#3886).

## What's Changed
* perf(patcher): traverse document elements linearly in O(n) by @twotnguyen in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3890
* build(deps-dev): bump @vitest/ui from 5.0.5 to 5.1.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3889
* build(deps-dev): bump vitest from 5.0.5 to 5.1.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3887
* build(deps-dev): bump globals from 17.13.0 to 17.14.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3884
* build(deps-dev): bump parse5 from 8.0.1 to 8.1.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3885
* build(deps-dev): bump @vitest/coverage-v8 from 5.0.5 to 5.1.0 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3888
* chore: Version bump to 9.15.3 by @dolanmiu in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3891

## New Contributors
* @twotnguyen made their first contribution in https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/pull/3890

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/compare/9.15.2...9.15.3

Easily generate and modify .docx files with JS/TS. Works for Node and on the Browser.

--- [![NPM version][npm-image]][npm-url] [![Downloads per month][downloads-image]][downloads-url] [![GitHub Action Workflow Status][github-actions-workflow-image]][github-actions-workflow-url] [![Known Vulnerabilities][snky-image]][snky-url] [![PRs Welcome][pr-image]][pr-url] [![codecov][codecov-image]][codecov-url] [![Docx.js Editor][docxjs-editor-image]][docxjs-editor-url]

# Demo ## Browser With basic `HTML/JS` in a browser, load `docx`'s browser build, which defines a global `docx`: ```html ``` Here are examples of `docx` working in `Angular`: - https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-docx - https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-wmd6k3 Here are examples of `docx` working in `React`: - https://stackblitz.com/edit/react-docx - https://stackblitz.com/edit/react-docx-images (adding images to Word Document) Here is an example of `docx` working in `Vue.js`: - https://stackblitz.com/edit/vuejs-docx ## Node Press `endpoint` on the `RunKit` website: ![RunKit Instructions](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2917613/38582539-f84311b6-3d07-11e8-90db-5885ae02c3c4.png) - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo1 - Simple paragraph and text - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo2 - Advanced Paragraphs and text - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo3 - Bullet points - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo4 - Simple table - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo5 - Images - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo6 - Margins - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo7 - Landscape - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo8 - Header and Footer - https://runkit.com/dolanmiu/docx-demo10 - **My CV generated with docx** More [here](https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/tree/master/demo) # How to use & Documentation Please refer to the [documentation at https://docx.js.org/](https://docx.js.org/) for details on how to use this library, examples and much more! # Shapes, watermarks and charts Shapes, groups of shapes and diagrams with connectors come with `docx`, from `docx/shapes`, watermarks from `docx/watermarks`, and native Word charts from `docx/charts`. They are left out of `docx` itself, so documents that don't use them don't carry their code: ```ts import { Document, Header, Paragraph } from "docx"; import { ChartRun } from "docx/charts"; import { ShapeRun } from "docx/shapes"; import { TextWatermark } from "docx/watermarks"; const doc = new Document({ sections: [ { headers: { default: new Header({ children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextWatermark({ text: "DRAFT" })] })] }) }, children: [ new Paragraph({ children: [new ShapeRun({ type: "ellipse", transformation: { width: 100, height: 60 } })] }), new Paragraph({ children: [new ChartRun({ type: "column", categories: ["Q1", "Q2"], series: [{ name: "Sales", values: [10, 20] }] })], }), ], }, ], }); ``` In a page without a bundler, load `dist/shapes.umd.cjs`, `dist/watermarks.umd.cjs` or `dist/charts.umd.cjs` after `dist/index.umd.cjs`. They add the `docxShapes`, `docxWatermarks` and `docxCharts` globals. See the [shapes](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/shapes), [watermarks](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/watermarks) and [charts](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/charts) documentation. # HTML HTML, such as what people write in a rich-text editor, becomes a document's paragraphs, lists, tables, images, links, equations and footnotes with `docx/html`, written in the document's own styles: ```ts import { Document } from "docx"; import { htmlToContent } from "docx/html"; const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: htmlToContent("

Report

Sales were up 12%.

  • EMEA
  • APAC
") }], }); ``` In a page without a bundler, load `dist/html.umd.cjs` after `dist/index.umd.cjs` and `dist/math.umd.cjs`. It adds the `docxHtml` global. See the [HTML](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/html) documentation. # Macros VBA macros, written from their code, make a document a macro-enabled document (`.docm`), with `docx/macros`: ```ts import { Document, Paragraph } from "docx"; import { createMacros } from "docx/macros"; const doc = new Document({ macros: createMacros({ modules: [{ name: "Greetings", code: 'Sub SayHello()\n MsgBox "Hello"\nEnd Sub' }], }), sections: [{ children: [new Paragraph("Run SayHello from View > Macros")] }], }); ``` In a page without a bundler, load `dist/macros.umd.cjs` after `dist/index.umd.cjs`. It adds the `docxMacros` global. See the [macros](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/macros) documentation. # Embedded Files Workbooks, documents, presentations and any other file, such as a sound, a video or a PDF, are embedded in a document as OLE objects, which open from it, with `docx/embedded-files`: ```ts import * as fs from "fs"; import { Document, Paragraph } from "docx"; import { EmbeddedFileRun } from "docx/embedded-files"; const doc = new Document({ sections: [ { children: [ new Paragraph({ children: [ new EmbeddedFileRun({ fileName: "budget.xlsx", data: fs.readFileSync("./budget.xlsx"), preview: { type: "png", data: fs.readFileSync("./budget.png") }, transformation: { width: 240, height: 120 }, }), ], }), ], }, ], }); ``` In a page without a bundler, load `dist/embedded-files.umd.cjs` after `dist/index.umd.cjs`. It adds the `docxEmbeddedFiles` global. See the [embedded files](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/embedded-files) documentation. # Citations and Bibliography Sources, citations of them in the text and a bibliography, in one of Word's styles of citation, such as APA, MLA or Chicago, written as Word writes them, with `docx/bibliography`: ```ts import { Document, Paragraph, TextRun } from "docx"; import { Bibliography, Citation, CitationStyle, SourceType, createBibliography } from "docx/bibliography"; const doc = new Document({ bibliography: createBibliography({ style: CitationStyle.APA, sources: [ { tag: "Bak10", type: SourceType.BOOK, authors: [{ lastName: "Baker", firstName: "Anna" }], title: "The Art of Pizza", year: 2010, city: "Naples", publisher: "Oven Press", }, ], }), sections: [ { children: [ new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Pizza has been baked in Naples for centuries "), new Citation("Bak10")] }), new Bibliography({ title: "References" }), ], }, ], }); ``` In a page without a bundler, load `dist/bibliography.umd.cjs` after `dist/index.umd.cjs`. It adds the `docxBibliography` global. See the [citations and bibliography](https://docx.js.org/#/usage/bibliography) documentation. # Playground Experience `docx` in action through [Docx.js Editor][docxjs-editor-url], an interactive playground where you can code and preview the results in real-time. # Examples Check the [demo folder](https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx/tree/master/demo) for examples. # Contributing Read the contribution guidelines [here](https://docx.js.org/#/contribution-guidelines). # Used by [](https://hfour.com/) [](https://fuzzproductions.com/) [](https://www.mettzer.com/) [](https://www.wisedoc.net/) [](https://www.dabblewriter.com/) [](https://turbopatent.com/) [](http://www.madisoncres.com/) [](https://www.beekast.com/) [](https://herraizsoto.com/) [](http://www.ativer.com.br/) [](https://www.arity.co/) [](https://www.circadianrisk.com/) [](https://lexense.com/) [](https://novelpad.co/) [](https://proton.me/) ...and many more!
